observations.pairA_difference: In 9E15 the dark card's top edge blends directly into the menu bar with no gap (a soft gradient transition from the menu bar's grey into the card's black, rows ~38-44 in the image); in C6D3 the menu bar ends with a hard edge and there is a visible strip of desktop grey between the menu bar and the card's top edge before the card begins (rows ~44-49), so the card sits detached, lower down.
observations.pairB_difference: Same structural difference as pair A: in 4B8A the panel's top edge blends into the menu bar with a gradient transition and no gap; in F03E there is a visible sliver of desktop grey between the menu bar and the panel's top edge, so the panel reads as a separate block floating below the menu bar.
observations.content_lost: No, all text and elements (labels, icons, buttons, checklist rows, source pills) appear identical within each pair; only the vertical attachment/gap to the menu bar differs.

why.pairA: 9E15's card visually fuses with the menu bar (no seam), so it reads as an extension of the top edge rather than a window sitting on the desktop; C6D3 leaves a strip of desktop grey between menu bar and card, which reads as a distinct floating panel.
why.pairB: Same logic as pair A: 4B8A's panel merges into the menu bar with no gap, reinforcing that it belongs to the screen's top edge, while F03E's visible gap makes it read as a separate app window hovering below the menu bar.
